items.text: PRACTICAL: MEASURING ENTHALPY CHANGES FOR DISPLACEMENT REACTIONS

items.label: text
items.text: In order to determine the enthalpy change of the reaction of zinc and copper(ll) sulfate, the following procedure could be used:

items.label: list_item
items.text: Place a polystyrene cup in a 250 cm³ glass beaker.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Transfer 50 cm³ of 0.200 mol/dm³ copper(Il) sulfate solution into the polystyrene cup using a measuring cylinder.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Weigh 1.20 g of zinc using a weighing boat on a balance.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Record the initial temperature of the copper(ll) sulfate solution.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Add the zinc.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Stir the solution as quickly as possible.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Record the maximum temperature reached.

items.label: text
items.text: 19.12 A calorimetry experiment to measure the enthalpy change of a displacement reaction.

items.label: table
items.text:
| initial temperature of copper(ll) sulfate solution/°C   |   17.0 |
|---------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| maximum temperature of the reaction mixture/°C          |   27.3 |

items.label: text
items.text: We can use this data to calculate the enthalpy change for this displacement reaction, when1 mole of copper(Il) sulfate reacts with zinc.

items.label: text
items.text: Heat given out in this reaction: Q = mc∆T = 50 × 4.18 × (27.3 - 17.0)

items.label: text
items.text: Here we assume the following:

items.label: list_item
items.text: The density of the copper sulfate solution is the same as that of water, so 1 cm³ of solution has a mass of 1g.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The specific heat capacity of the mixture is the same as that of water. This is a fairly reasonable assumption because the reaction mixture is mostly water.
